_comment: Public-suffix data, split by WHO CHOOSES THE LABEL BELOW THE SUFFIX. That distinction is what lets a detector know whether its assumptions apply; it is not a reputation judgement and grants no trust. PROTOTYPE SIMPLIFICATION: production should use the full Mozilla Public Suffix List via publicsuffix2, whose ICANN/PRIVATE sections map onto registry_suffixes/provider_suffixes directly.

registry_suffixes._comment: Multi-label REGISTRY suffixes. A registrant picks the label below these and pays for it, so the label carries intent.

provider_suffixes._comment: Hosting/PaaS namespaces (the PSL 'private' section). The label below these is allocated inside a provider's own namespace - often machine-generated - so a model calibrated on registrant-chosen brand labels is out of distribution here. Listing a provider does NOT make it trusted: threat intelligence, behavioural, tunnelling and brand/keyword signals are unaffected.

special_use_suffixes._comment: RFC 6761/7686/8375 special-use names, split by HOW NAMES IN THE ZONE ARE CHOSEN. 'unregistered' zones hold device and host names nobody registered, so registrant-label analysis is meaningless. 'registrant_shaped' zones are reserved for documentation and testing but hold ordinary registrant-style labels, so they are analysed as normal registry domains - this project's own fixtures use .test and .invalid.

infrastructure_suffixes._comment: DNS operational zones. Labels are operator-defined or encode an address; they are never registrant-chosen.
